instrument: 195 FERC ¶ 61,216; Docket EL26-69-000; Order Instituting Proceeding Under Section 206 of the Federal Power Act
jurisdiction_or_scope: United States interstate transmission; NYISO show-cause order using PJM precedent
service_or_claim: interim NITS and firm/non-firm contract-demand transmission service up to a specified MW contract level
trigger_or_matching_rule: flexible large loads may limit withdrawals under specified conditions; approved withdrawal level is enforced by control/protection systems, potentially including a special protection scheme
physical_resource_boundary: net energy withdrawal at the transmission-service boundary and its approved MW level; the order does not identify internal computing tasks
what_it_supports: network-side contractual and operational curtailment is a distinct institutional object, and MW-limited transmission service can depend on verifiable withdrawal control
what_it_does_not_support: does not establish an hourly CFE claim, does not identify a data center that also makes such a claim, and does not prove simultaneous use of the same workload flexibility or its frequency

jurisdiction_or_scope: voluntary granular-certificate schemes; electricity consumption claims
service_or_claim: temporal, geographical, and attribute matching of canceled granular certificates to measured consumption
trigger_or_matching_rule: matching is ex-post after consumption data and certificates are available; consumption volume must be covered by certificates from the same interval, at least hourly, using hourly/sub-hourly production and consumption data
physical_resource_boundary: metered energy consumption and certificate attributes within the declared temporal/geographical matching framework; not controllable load capacity
what_it_supports: hourly/sub-hourly CFE accounting and claim verification are distinct institutional processes with explicit time-interval and metering rules
what_it_does_not_support: does not create a network emergency-service obligation, does not establish physically dispatchable workload capacity, and does not prove dual contracting or common-envelope use

jurisdiction_or_scope: Google corporate operations and methodological guidance
service_or_claim: 24/7 CFE goal and framework for matching operational electricity consumption when and where it occurs
trigger_or_matching_rule: corporate methodology defines and measures progress toward location- and time-matched CFE
physical_resource_boundary: facility electricity consumption and attributable regional CFE under the corporate methodology; not an emergency-response capacity product
what_it_supports: a data-center operator can maintain a corporate hourly CFE accounting/procurement framework separate from transmission-service rules
what_it_does_not_support: does not show that a named facility has pledged the same flexible workload to a network-side contract, does not measure contract-overlap incidence, and is not regulatory certification

instrument: The Internet is 24x7—carbon-free energy should be too
jurisdiction_or_scope: Google data centers and regional electricity markets
service_or_claim: hourly matching of each facility's electricity use with regional carbon-free supply, counting regional PPAs and the regional grid mix
trigger_or_matching_rule: facility load is evaluated hour by hour against regional PPA generation; unmatched load is attributed to the regional grid mix
physical_resource_boundary: hourly facility consumption and regional attributable CFE; PPA electricity is mixed in the grid rather than exclusively delivered to the data center
what_it_supports: provides an official data-center example linking hourly facility consumption, regional CFE, and long-term PPAs
what_it_does_not_support: does not establish a network-contingent service contract, physical curtailment deliverability, simultaneous commitment of one workload envelope, or an overlap probability
